- snipedstudio.com · 4.7% · KEEP
- brycedenphoto.com · 4.5% · KEEP
- snipedproduction.com · 2.0% · MONITOR (run inbox placement test, re-warm if needed)
- snipedvisuals.com · 0.8% · PAUSE + re-warm 14 days
- admin@snipedmedia.com · 0% (24 sent) · KILL FROM COLD · primary business email, never use again
Voice rules (locked, lifetime):
- NO EM DASHES. Use colon, middle dot, comma, parentheses, arrow, two sentences.
- Plain text only. No HTML, images, links in body.
- Signature: name + website only.
- 5th-7th grade reading level. Hemingway / Flesch-Kincaid 70+.
- Under 80 words per email.
- One CTA per email.
- Lowercase casual subject lines. No title case, no caps lock.
- No buzzwords, no corporate tone, no 'great post' energy.
- Mid-conversation feel. Slight imperfection is the goal.
- Don't lead with my expertise. Lead with the observation.
- Operator voice: texture, not clinical perfection. The slightly broken-on-purpose copy converts.

SNIPED runs TWO outbound channels in parallel. Different ICPs, different mechanics.
LinkedIn VIB lane · precision spear:
- ICP: LA tech FOUNDERS (Tier 0 CRM, sourced manually by Ren)
- Volume: 4-6 VIBs/week
- Asset: bespoke VIB PNG (LEFT prospect photo / RIGHT matched SNIPED reference)
- Mechanics: personalized DM with VIB attached, 1:1 conversation
- Conversion: VIB → reply → call → Reset
Cold email lane · volume net:
- ICP: LA tech VPs / Directors / non-founder C-Suite (Tier 1-4 by trigger count)
- Volume: ~150 emails/day (~750/week, ~3000/month)
- Asset: 3-email sequence + Loom audit on positive reply
- Mechanics: high-volume automated send with personalized line 1, templated body
- Conversion: email 1 → reply → Loom delivered → call → Reset
Zero cannibalization rule:
- Cold email targets NEVER include founders (those go to LinkedIn VIB)
- LinkedIn VIB targets NEVER include random VPs without a referral relationship (those go to cold email)
- Cross-check suppression lists across both channels before any new pull
Combined funnel target Phase 1: $3K MRR sustained 2 months = 2 Resets/week from combined channels.

Every chapter runs 3 to 5 grid posts depending on look count. Composite HERO is mandatory. Chapter Card is mandatory. Card is always an IG Collab post with the subject. Captions are minimal and ritualized ([FirstName] · [##]). Breathing gap is 1 to 3 days between chapters. No fake daily posting. Rhythm: escalation → climax → closure → silence → re-entry.
Universal sequence:
[1 frame per look · capped at 3] → [Composite HERO · mandatory] → [Chapter Card · mandatory · always collab post] → [Breathing gap · 1 to 3 days] → [Next chapter]
No subject tiers. Model, casting-call collaborator, founder, lineage figure, self-shoot: same structure. Chapter doesn't ask 'who is this person.' It asks 'how many looks did the shoot produce.'
Rollout by look count:
- 1 look = 1 build + HERO + Card = 3 posts
- 2 looks = 2 builds + HERO + Card = 4 posts
- 3 looks = 3 builds + HERO + Card = 5 posts
- 4+ looks = 3 (cap) + HERO + Card = 5 posts (cap)
Why cap builds at 3: Hit Makers exposure mechanic — audience needs repetition to recognize subject, but more than 3 build frames before HERO collapses the climax. Three is the sweet spot.

Each post type gets a visually different caption so audience reads chapter structure instantly:
- Look frame (build): [FirstName] · [##] · e.g. 'Yae · 01', 'Yae · 02'
- HERO (climax): [FirstName] · [Environment] · e.g. 'Yae · Brutalist Monument'
- HERO (when not introducing new environment): [FirstName] · [##] · e.g. 'Yae · 03'
- Chapter Card (closure): Chapter ## · e.g. 'Chapter 01'
Three shapes serve three jobs: numbered = build (subject + sequence). Subject + Environment = climax (subject + world). Standalone Chapter # = closure (sealed).
Universal caption rules (every post):
- First name only (full name only in subject credit field)
- Number = sequential post in chapter
- No editorial note in caption, no adjectives, no questions, no emoji
- No hashtags in caption itself (3 max in first comment if used, SNIPED-specific only)
- No CTA, no 'link in bio'
- Subject IG handle goes in FIRST COMMENT, not caption
- Other credits (MUA, location, composite credit) go in first comment
Why credits in first comment: keeps grid caption visually clean across all chapters. Audience trains on convention over 5-10 chapters and recognizes [FirstName] · [##] AS the SNIPED chapter system itself.

Chapter Cards render image in BLACK & WHITE. HERO post remains full color (v3 LUXURY).
Dual-register rule:
- HERO = the moment. Color. Cinematic. World-building. v3 LUXURY locked palette. Chapter's climax in full color.
- Card = the document. B&W. Archival. Canonization. Chapter sealed into SNIPED archive.
Doctrinally: B&W treatment is APPARATUS LAYER, not edit style change. Lock 7 ('v3 LUXURY is the only editing style') governs source image edit. Card displays a desaturated version for artifact treatment — source image remains v3 LUXURY color. Same convention as Aperture, LIFE, Magnum publishing color work in B&W on archival monographs.
Implementation:
- Saturation: -1 (full desaturation)
- Contrast: +0.08 (slight bump for editorial punch)
- Exposure: +0.02 (tiny lift)
- Applied as Figma image fill filter on IMAGE_DROP_ZONE of Card template
- Alternative: pre-desaturate source in Lightroom before uploading
Masthead apparatus stays color: paper warm bg (#F5EFE6), black SNIPED wordmark, brass-darker colophon (#8B6E50), brass hairline rules + BJ signature glyph. Apparatus carries warm-cool tension; photograph carries archival register.
Tradition lineage: Aperture (monograph covers in B&W even when interiors color), LIFE (archival editions in B&W), Magnum (contact sheets and monograph editions in B&W), The Crisis (Du Bois era · intellectual seriousness through tonal restraint), The New Yorker (selective monochrome covers).

Pacing rule (operator-locked): every grid post gets at least one breath day after it. No two chapter posts on consecutive days. Applies to BUILD frames, HERO, and CARD equally. Breath day is the doctrine, not the exception.
Chapter arc (locked sequence):
Build 1 → breath → Build 2 → breath → [Build 3 → breath] → HERO → breath → CARD → breath → breath → next chapter opens
Why breath day between every post:
- Each frame holds its slot in feed instead of getting buried
- Grid reads as curated archive, not content firehose
- Reinforces 50% chapter exposure rule over 30-day window
- Audience trains on rhythm — they expect breath, silence becomes part of chapter
3-look chapter (5 grid posts · 11-day arc): Day 1 Build A → Day 2 breath → Day 3 Build B → Day 4 breath → Day 5 Build C → Day 6 breath → Day 7 HERO (collab) → Day 8 breath → Day 9 CARD (B&W collab) → Days 10-11 breath → Day 12 next chapter opens.
Audience fatigue defense:
- 50% chapter exposure rule: across any 30-day window, no more than 50% grid posts should be chapter content. Other 50% = single-frame portraits not tied to chapter, archived frames re-surfacing, process/methodology posts, cultural context, quiet recurring environment posts.
- Breathing gap NON-NEGOTIABLE. Min 1-day gap. Heavy chapters earn 5-7 days.
- No two HEROs within 7 days. Composite HEROs are visual peaks of entire account; stacking collapses peaks. Target one HERO every 7-14 days.
Bi-weekly cadence target: CH+1 HERO drops ~11 days after CH HERO. That holds bi-weekly minimum. Supports 16-chapter floor by 2026-12-31.

When picking the Chapter Card image from chapter selects (the Card is NEVER the HERO composite — it uses a different chapter frame, ideally most operator-coded business-fit frame):
1. Technical floor: sharp, properly exposed, free of artifacts
2. Register check: body language demonstrates composed authority (Direction Stack visible)
3. Eye check: eyes carry steadiness or intentional composed-away
4. Wardrobe + environment check: subject + environment + wardrobe read as one unit
5. Negative space check: frame has room for masthead and bottom imprint to breathe
6. The 10-year subject test: would the subject feel honored by this frame in 10 years?
7. Operator-coded preference: if multiple pass, pick one where subject is most operator-coded (composed business-fit register, less fashion-aesthetic)
What this doctrine BANS:
- Skipping the Chapter Card (mandatory)
- Skipping the composite HERO (mandatory)
- Using HERO composite as the Card image (Card uses different frame)
- Editorial copy in caption beyond locked patterns
- Subject-specific tier treatment (every subject = same structure)
- Posting during breathing gap (1-3 day silence minimum)
- More than one HERO per chapter
- Two HEROs within 7 days
- Hashtags in caption itself
- Aspirational copy ('elevated', 'luxury', 'premium', 'icon', 'boss')
- Engagement bait ('which look?', 'thoughts?')
- 'Link in bio' CTA in chapter post captions
- Themed issue titles (no 'Power Issue' franchise covers)

Every shoot gets one root folder, structured identically. Located on working SSD at /SNIPED_PRODUCTION/YYYY/.
/SNIPED_PRODUCTION/2026/2026-05-18_Sasha_FreeCollab/
  00_BRIEF/    · pre-shoot brief, contract, model release, mood ref
  10_RAW/      · untouched .CR3 files from SD card
  20_CULLED/   · Lightroom catalog (.lrcat) + smart previews
  30_HEROES/   · final retouched .tif (master) + .jpg (deliverable)
  40_SELECTS/  · color-graded .jpg only
  50_PROOFS/   · batch-graded .jpg only
  60_DELIVERY/ · Pixieset upload bundles (zipped per tier)
  70_BTS/      · phone footage (.mp4), still grabs, audio (.wav)
  80_CONTENT/  · Reel renders, carousel exports, captions.md
  90_NOTES/    · post-shoot notes
Locked. Every shoot produces all 9 subfolders even if some stay empty. Empty subfolders signal 'did not happen this shoot,' not 'lost in system.'
Workspace separation:
- /SNIPED_OS/ — operating system (strategy + SOPs)
- /SNIPED_PRODUCTION/ — all shoot assets (separate)
- /SNIPED_ARCHIVE/ — cold storage (mirrored HDD)
- /SNIPED_CONTENT_LIBRARY/ — evergreen content templates + ready-to-post
Critical: SNIPED_OS is separate from SNIPED_PRODUCTION. Assets do not pollute OS folder. Strategy does not pollute asset folder.

Shoot folder: YYYY-MM-DD_ClientLastName_TYPE
Type values: Reset / Sprint / OpKit / BrandSystem / FreeCollab / FreeCommunity / FreeAccess / Personal / ArtSeries / CulturalDoc / BTSDay
Example: 2026-06-15_DavisLaw_Reset
File names within folders:
- Hero (master): SNIPED_2026-06-15_DavisLaw_HERO_001.tif
- Hero (deliverable): SNIPED_2026-06-15_DavisLaw_HERO_001.jpg
- Select: SNIPED_2026-06-15_DavisLaw_SEL_001.jpg
- Proof: SNIPED_2026-06-15_DavisLaw_PRF_001.jpg
- BTS clip: SNIPED_2026-06-15_DavisLaw_BTS_001.mp4
- Carousel: SNIPED_2026-06-15_DavisLaw_CAR-IG_01.jpg
SNIPED prefix lets you find any file from global search. No spaces, no special characters except hyphens and underscores. Never rename a RAW file. Only outputs get the SNIPED naming pattern.
Storage tiering:
- Hot (working SSD 1-2TB Samsung T7 / SanDisk Extreme Pro): last 60 days, current edits. $100-200.
- Warm (8TB external HDD Seagate/WD): last 12 months, all delivered. $150.
- Cold (8TB mirror HDD, stored at home NOT in studio bag): year+ archive. $150.
- Cloud (Backblaze B2 OR rclone to Google Drive): everything from /30_HEROES/ + /50_PROOFS/ + /80_CONTENT/. $5-15/mo.
RAW files live on Hot+Warm only. Cloud cost too high for RAW backup vs recovery value.
3-2-1 backup discipline (modified for cost): SD → Hot SSD → Warm HDD mirror via rsync. Card stays full and unformatted until both copies verified. Every 90 days, attempt restore one random shoot from cold or cloud to verify backups work.

topic: Photo pipeline · ingest → cull → edit time targets
content:
Ingest (15 min after every shoot, same day, non-negotiable):
1. Card → USB-C reader (no laptop card slot · slower)
2. Photo Mechanic Plus auto-import OR Lightroom Classic import to /10_RAW/
3. Verify file count matches camera display
4. Run rsync to mirror HDD
5. Confirm both copies bit-identical
6. Eject card, label 'DO NOT FORMAT' until next shoot day
Cull (15-25 min, same day or next morning):
- Pass 0 (auto): AI auto-rejects OOF, eyes-closed, blink, exposure failures (Lightroom Assisted Culling at import) — saves 30-45 min
- Pass 1: reject refinement (5-8 min). 'X' key.
- Pass 2: pick pass (8-12 min). 'P' key.
- Pass 3: star pass (5-10 min). Number keys. 3=Proof, 4=Select, 5=Hero candidate.
- Pass 4: color label (2-3 min). On 5-star: Red (heavy retouch · Photoshop), Yellow (standard pipeline · Evoto), Blue (VIB pool), Purple (case study), Green (delivered)
Hero edit (12-15 min/Hero target):
1. Lightroom locked-look applied on import (SNIPED_LOCKED_LOOK_v1)
2. Per-image develop in locked order
3. AI mask stack: 5 masks (Subject, Face Skin, Eyes, Teeth, Background)
4. Generative Remove for in-LR cleanup
5. Decision tree: Yellow → Evoto, Red → Photoshop
6. Apply SNIPED_HERO_FINISH_v1 preset after Evoto round-trip
7. Export via SNIPED · Hero · JPG Deliverable + TIF Master presets
8. Topaz Photo AI sharpen on .jpg only
9. After delivery, color label → Green
If Hero exceeds 25 min: stop, ship as-is or downgrade to Select. Time-cap discipline > perfection.
Select edit: 1-2 min/Select. NO Evoto, NO Photoshop. Lightroom base preset + color grading + export.
Proof edit: 30-45 sec/Proof. Lightroom batch. SNIPED Proofs preset. 100 proofs × 45 sec = 75 min.

topic: AI tool routing · Camp B rule
content:
Camp B rule (absolute): AI tools generate INPUTS (backgrounds, moodboards, plates, references). AI tools NEVER generate the subject's face, body, hair, or identity.
Photo AI stack:
- Lightroom Classic: cull, base color, tone, masked adjustments, Generative Remove for in-LR cleanup. Every shoot.
- Evoto: skin retouch + body subtle + backdrop color/replace + AI Color Match (batch style propagation) + AI Color Looks + frequency separation (Brand System tier) + sculpt D&B + AI Transform + tethered shooting. Every Hero.
- Topaz Photo AI: sharpening + denoise on output, upscaling AI background plates. Hero export step + Track B comp upscaling.
- Photoshop: final compositing, frequency separation, Track B AI-background-plate assembly (Neural Filter Harmonize + edge lights + grain + color wash per Gress 5-step playbook). Red-label frames + Brand System + Track B creative push.
- Adobe Firefly: background plate generation (cityscape, atmospheric, beach, color wash). Track B only.
- Google Nano Banana Pro (via Gemini/Freepik): narrative scene plates (stadium, hotel, urban, tunnel). Track B.
- Midjourney: stylized/artistic register only. Track B.
- Capture One: color-critical commercial work (Op Kit, Brand System). Phase B+ option.
What NEVER gets outsourced (to AI or humans):
- Direction Stack diagnostic on every shoot
- 90-second on-set opener
- Pricing decision (holding the price)
- Methodology refinement
- Year-10 vision decisions
- Top-network relationship conversations (Larry, Pearl, Tracy, top 5 client referrers)
- Aesthetic call (which frames make Hero, Select, Proof)
- The decision to decline
- Substack essay voice (Q3+)
- Book authorship
What SHOULD be delegated to AI ASAP: Hero edit retouch (Evoto already), caption first drafts (Claude), email first drafts, pre-shoot brief drafting, Notion DB property formula construction, Reel auto-captions, color batch processing (Lightroom presets), LinkedIn POV scheduling decisions (use bank rotation, no AI needed).

Every Reset is briefed pre-shoot to produce these outputs, not just client gallery.
BTS capture during shoot day:
- 3 setup shots (lighting being adjusted, modifiers, empty set)
- 2 subject-arrives moments (handshake, intro)
- 5 in-action clips (directing, subject reacting, protocol diagnostic moment)
- 2 between-frames clips (subject relaxing, in-between moment)
- 1 final-frame moment (last shot taken)
Total: ~15 clips, 5-15 sec each. Phone clipped to small tripod or handheld by MUA / Pearl / collaborator. NO talking-to-camera Bryce footage during paid client shoots (client experience first); talking-head captured on dedicated BTS Content Days.
Reel production (BTS Cut format, 30-60 sec): CapCut on iPad/laptop. 6-9 clips, 3-7 sec each. Music: locked rotation of 5-7 tracks from CapCut royalty-free pool (build once, reuse · brand consistency). No text overlays beyond opening name/title card. Color grade clips to match SNIPED palette. Export 1080×1920 .mp4. Target: 30-45 min/Reel.
IG Carousel: Slot 1 = Hero frame 1080×1350. Slots 2-7 = 4-6 additional Heroes/context. Slot 8 = closing card (matte black with one-line CTA). Build in Figma OR pre-built Lightroom export preset.
LinkedIn POV: 1 Hero from /30_HEROES/ cropped to 1080×1350. Caption per LinkedIn POV bank rotation. Posted Tue or Thu, 7-9 AM PT.
Caption framework scaffold:
HOOK (one line · the protocol or insight named)
CONTEXT (3-5 lines · why it matters)
DEPLOYMENT (1-2 lines · where this shows up in buyer's reality)
CTA or close (1 line · 'DM SNIPED for the diagnostic' or just '·')
Repost / recycle: LinkedIn POV from 6 mo ago → repost with one updated insight. IG Carousel hero frames → re-used as LinkedIn single-frame after 90 days. BTS Reel → cropped to 9:16 still and posted as IG single after 30 days. Cultural Doc carousel → essay-formatted Substack post (Q3+) after 60 days.

topic: Delegation permission matrix + retoucher hire trigger
content:
First hire candidate: Retoucher (Mo 6-9). Trigger: edit-hours-per-Reset moving average crosses 5 hours OR 4+ Resets booked in same month.
Tools required: Lightroom Classic + Evoto + Photoshop (own subscriptions, BJ does not provision). Adobe license remains BJ's.
Cloud access (Dropbox folder $12/mo per shoot):
- Read+write on /20_CULLED/ and /30_HEROES/ for active shoot only
- NO access to /00_BRIEF/ (contains client brief + contract), /SNIPED_OS/, Notion CRM, Pixieset, Stripe
Tasks: Retouch passes 1-3 on every Hero. Apply SNIPED Evoto preset stack. Output .tif master to /30_HEROES/. Slack/Notion message: 'Heroes pass 3 complete on [Shoot ID].'
BJ retains: Pass 4 (final aesthetic call), Hero count selection, final .jpg export, Pixieset upload, delivery email.
QC: BJ reviews every Hero before Pixieset upload. Reject criteria: skin retouch over-smoothed (loss of texture), backdrop AI artifacting, color shift from base preset. Three rejected Heroes in one shoot triggers retoucher conversation.
Indicative cost: $40-80/Hero or $30-50/hour. Budget for 10-12 Heroes/Reset = $400-960/Reset. Reset margin remains $500-1000 after fee.
Other future hires (Mo 9-12+): Content/Reel editor (trigger ≥4 Reels/wk for 1 month), Social media VA (trigger $5K/mo × 2 + content-bottleneck), General VA (trigger BJ at admin/calendar/research-bottleneck for 2 weeks), Bookkeeper (Mo 9+ OR first $5K month).
Permission matrix legend: RW = read+write, R = read only, n/a = no access. BJ keeps RW everywhere. Other roles get scoped access only to what they need to do their specific job.

Architecture compresses into 6 running loops. If these run, SNIPED compounds. If any stops, system limps. Everything else = supporting infrastructure.
| # | Loop | Engine | Frequency | Owner | Surface | Compounding asset |
| L1 | VIB Loop | Revenue | Weekly (6 sends) | BJ | LinkedIn DM + Notion Outreach | Pipeline + referrals + positioning |
| L2 | Reset Loop | Revenue | Per-booking (target 2-4/mo) | BJ | Calendly→Studio→Pixieset→Day-0/1/2 upsell | Revenue + case studies + hero archive |
| L3 | Authority Loop | Audience | Weekly (1 LinkedIn POV) | BJ | LinkedIn (Tue/Thu 7-9 AM PT) + 5 founder comments | Audience trust + DM warm layer + methodology visibility |
| L4 | Cultural Documentation Loop | Reputation | Monthly (quarterly Phase 1) | BJ + editor | IG carousel + Substack essay (Q3+) | Body-of-work archive + institutional trust + AI-proof moat |
| L5 | Day-30 Loop | Revenue | Per-delivered-Reset | BJ | DM thread + Op Kit pitch | Op Kit conversions + relationship deepening |
| L6 | Constraint Audit Loop | Operations | Monthly (last Monday) | BJ | Notion review + 1 page decision | Compounding focus + drift correction |
Notion's Operator Dashboard page = single visualization for L1-L5. Constraint Audit (L6) = single decision artifact that meta-runs the other five.
If you remove any loop, identify what fills the gap before removing. System brittle to skipping; robust to slowing.

These are sacred. Delegating them collapses the brand.
1. Direction Stack diagnostic on every shoot. The 10-protocol named-correction is what people pay $1,500 for. Delegating = becoming a generic studio.
2. The on-set 90-second opener. Trust-build that decides next 45 minutes. Cannot be subcontracted.
3. The pricing decision. Holding the price. Refusing the discount. Walking from wrong-tier work.
4. Methodology refinement. Updates to Direction Stack, Aesthetic v2/v3, Production Stack. IP can only evolve through operator who lives it.
5. The Year-10 vision. What game is being played. Which opportunities serve it.
6. Relationship-deepening conversations with top 5-10 network nodes (Larry, Pearl, Bishop Peters, Tracy, future Op Kit clients).
7. The aesthetic call. Which frames make gallery, become Selected Work, become Art Series. Editorial judgment.
8. The decision to decline. Wrong-tier client, conflicting brand, free-shoot-no-return. Saying no protects the moat.
9. Substack essay voice (Q3 2026+). The writing IS the credential. Cannot be ghost-written.
10. Book authorship. Direction Stack + future books. Ghost-written = generic = brand-killing.
Everything else is delegate-able with the right system. The discipline is recognizing where the line is.

Patterns that signal slipping, with named correctives.
1. Overthinking · Signs: 5+ tabs of references before starting, 30+ min talking through decision, adding to strategy doc instead of shipping next move, re-reading Operating Brief weekly. Corrective: 2-min timer. Make decision. Ship. Operating Brief reread quarterly, not weekly.
2. Emotionally avoiding · Signs: choosing edit over outreach (edit feels productive; outreach feels exposed), choosing planning over executing, 'I need to research this more first', spending Mon Protected Hour on anything except VIB production. Corrective: name avoidance OUT LOUD. Ship the avoided thing FIRST today. Discomfort = signal this is the high-leverage work.
3. Wrong game · Signs: checking IG analytics multiple times/day, comparing follower counts to other LA photographers, feeling 'behind' relative to creator-economy peers, tempted by viral-format content. Corrective: re-read REVERSE_ROADMAP Section 0. Close analytics tab. Do one thing today that produces archive value, not metric value.
4. Drifting from moat · Signs: considering wedding/family/lifestyle gig 'this one time', saying yes to brand whose values conflict with operator-coded thesis, discounting Reset price to close, accepting free shoot without written return mechanic. Corrective: re-read content philosophy Section 6. Decline wrong-tier work even at short-term cost.
5. Underprepared · Signs: pre-shoot brief not sent at 24h, contract not signed before shoot date, arriving studio less than 60 min before client, edit running into Day 5 SLA without buffer. Corrective: pre-flight checklist Friday for upcoming week's shoots. Anything missing → Monday Protected Hour fixes.
6. Motion confused with progress · Signs: producing 5+ posts/week with no VIBs sent, spending 4+ hr on workspace docs/week with no Reset shipped, 'updating the system' feels like rewarding accomplishment. Corrective: Compounding-vs-Motion Audit weekly if drift detected.
7. Engineering job creeping into SNIPED time · Signs: SNIPED Mon Protected Hour repeatedly skipped, engineering travel weeks expanding, choosing engineering OT over SNIPED execution. Corrective: engineering job is funding mechanism, not priority. If hours systematically displaced, engineer income trajectory needs review.
8. Relationship infrastructure neglected · Signs: 14+ days since meaningful Pearl conversation about non-logistics, 60+ days since touching Larry, 30+ days since non-transactional church/community presence. Corrective: schedule one unsolicited touch this week (delivered print, thoughtful email, coffee, non-logistics conversation).

Workspace must stay operationally clean over time without regenerating it.
Tier organization (locked structure):
Active surface (top of workspace, daily-weekly use):
- MONDAY_COCKPIT.md (weekly load surface)
- OPERATIONAL_BACKBONE.md (this doc; reread quarterly)
- EXECUTION_PRIORITIZATION.md (reread when prioritizing)
- Notion CRM Operator Dashboard
Reference surface (folders 02-08, used per-task): Contracts (per signing), Production SOPs (per shoot), Outreach SOPs (per VIB sprint), Content philosophy + video philosophy (per content production), Notion schemas (rare consultation after build).
Strategy depth (reread quarterly or annually):
- SNIPED_OS_OPERATING_BRIEF.md (read quarterly)
- REVERSE_ROADMAP.md (read quarterly)
- sniped_content_philosophy.md (read annually for refresh)
- cultural_documentation_thesis.md (read annually)
Source material (10_REFERENCE; cite-only, never re-read in full): The 13 Stacks, the 12 Playbooks, SOCIAL_MEDIA_3_0_REFERENCE, the 9 Studies + 9 Art Series files, Production OG manuals, reference books (PDF/EPUB).
Vault (99_VAULT; explicitly empty): reserved for future SNIPED-only IP concepts. Do not populate with externally-owned project worlds.
Quarterly archive sweep (last Monday of quarter, 15 min):
- Active-surface doc not touched in 90 days → reference
- Reference doc not touched in 180 days → 10_REFERENCE
- Planned-but-unwritten artifact still on 'to do' after 90 days → kill or commit
- Active-surface count should stay at ~5 docs maximum
The 'do not generate' rule: in future sessions, Claude maintains/surfaces/audits/condenses. Does NOT generate new strategy docs unless directed, re-architect existing systems unless user names a problem, produce framework deliverables for own sake.

topic: Seven laws of the working photography business
content:
1. The camera is a business tool. Not identity. Not art project. High-leverage tool that points at people, products, events, yourself. Each direction = different revenue model.
2. Price on outcomes, not hours. Client buys business result the photography produces (house sells quicker, listing converts, team page signals competence, album outlasts marriage). Price the result.
3. Niche down or stay broke. Generalists compete on price; specialists compete on expertise. Wedding specialist at $5,000 makes more than generalist charging $800. Pick one lane after testing four. Kill the others explicitly. Tell yourself out loud you are not taking those jobs anymore.
4. Active service funds the stack. Passive funds the freedom. Both streams run simultaneously. One funds the other.
5. Build revenue streams in sequence, not parallel. Active service first. Then gallery upsells. Then digital product. Then automated print store. Then licensing. Then affiliate. Then authority pivot. Each stream goes 'being built' → 'set and forget' before next starts.
6. Point the camera at yourself eventually. The photographers who hit real income are the ones who stop pointing camera exclusively at clients. Teaching, documenting process, building audience around the work. This is where 10K/mo becomes 30K/mo. Most avoid because requires showing your face.
7. The system is the moat. Talent is entry requirement, not differentiator. Pricing sheet that converts, intake process that qualifies fast, SOP that delivers consistently, funnel that refills itself, financial architecture that survives slow month. Nobody competes with a system they cannot see.

Pick four niches from working set (events, product/e-commerce, portraits/headshots, real estate, weddings, B2B retainer). Pick based on what you can access locally, NOT what sounds appealing.
- Shoot 3 projects in each over 60 days. 12 shoots total. Friends, family, low-cost clients, TFP if necessary. Shoots don't need to be paid; need to be real.
- Track 4 variables per niche: time to complete, total revenue, energy cost (1-10), portfolio yield (usable images).
- Pick the niche with HIGHEST RATIO of revenue+portfolio to energy cost. NOT the one you liked most. The one numbers pick.
- Kill other three. Stop taking inquiries. Marketing, portfolio, pricing collapse onto selected lane.
Test removes fantasy layer. Photographers who pick niche based on dreamed-about shoots end up in niche that drains them. Niche numbers pick = usually lowest friction in local market.
Niche of One: combine two seemingly unrelated interests/skills to create unique non-competitive segment.
- Wedding photographer who shoots medium format film. Two variables = narrower pool, higher rates, fewer direct competitors.
- Product photographer specializing in food + chef portraits. Two angles on restaurant industry. One relationship, two invoices.
- Portrait photographer for lawyers and law firms. One vertical where decision-makers talk to each other.
- Real estate + drone video walkthroughs. Two deliverables bundled.
The gap between two adjacent skills = pricing power. Nobody else at that crossroads. Pricing no longer a comparison.
Specialization math: generalist at $800 × 3 shoots/wk = $124,800/yr. Specialist at $2,500 × 1 shoot/wk = $130,000/yr. Same revenue, 1/3 shoots, 2× margin, infinitely less burnout.

3-tier anchor structure on every pricing sheet:
- Tier 1 Entry: bread-and-butter, low barrier, quick turnaround. Minimum deliverables. Should feel like a steal vs Tier 2.
- Tier 2 Value: the package you actually want them to buy. Best balance deliverables + margin. Full session, edited images, 1-2 premium add-ons. Priced ~60-70% of Tier 3.
- Tier 3 Home Run: premium anchor. Every add-on bundled. Exists to make Tier 2 look reasonable. Priced ~2× Tier 2.
Most clients buy Tier 2. Tier 3 not there to be bought — there to make Tier 2 read as sensible. Tier 1 catches inquiries who would have walked away.
Pricing rules:
1. Round numbers only. $2,160 not $2,159.99. Round = intention. Decimals = discount stores.
2. Drop commas. $2160 reads smaller than $2,160. Comma anchors price into 'thousands' range. Remove and number scans less imposing.
3. Never lower prices. If client can't afford quoted package, do not drop price. REMOVE DELIVERABLES. Price holds. Deliverables adjust.
4. Ask the budget first. 'What budget are you working with?' Let client define scope before quoting. Most have a number in mind.
5. Price the outcome, not the input. 'This session produces full visual infrastructure your new website needs' justifies $1,500. '$250/hr × 6 hours + 2 hr editing' justifies whatever client's internal hourly comparison produces.
The pricing equation: Time + Deliverables + Equipment + Experience = Package Value. When raising prices, ask which variable changed. If none, raise may not hold. If one (new gear, portfolio milestone, case study), raise is defensible.

Wage separation system:
- All revenue pools into dedicated business account (NOT personal, NOT joint).
- Pay business expenses first. Gear. Software. Lab. Studio. Taxes.
- Pay yourself FIXED weekly salary from business account. Same amount every week regardless of week's revenue. Slow week ≠ small paycheck. Huge week ≠ huge paycheck.
- Remainder stays in business account as profit. Reinvested into gear, scaling, or passive stream buildout.
- Survival baseline: total annual personal living costs ÷ 52. If average weekly business revenue can't cover year-round, you don't have a full-time business yet. You have a paying side project.
The separation = single biggest psychological shift in running a photography business. Slow weeks stop being existential crises. Fast weeks stop funding lifestyle inflation.
Four wealth levels:
1. Survival: income covers expenses. No margin for error. Decisions reactive. Bad month = crisis.
2. Stability: $10K cash reserve, 30 days funded ahead. First time you can turn down a bad client.
3. Growth: active income ~2× burn rate. Surplus compounds. Pricing raises possible without fear.
4. Freedom: passive income exceeds burn rate. Labor is optional. Every shoot a choice.
$10K reserve = single most important financial milestone. Until in account, every other financial decision distorted by survival thinking. Eliminates 'I need this booking' panic. Discipline: cut every non-essential expense. Every surplus dollar to reserve until $10K. Nothing else (no gear upgrades, no lifestyle expansion, no investments) until reserve hit.
Tax discipline: set aside 25-30% of EVERY incoming payment for taxes. Not at tax time — at deposit time. Money moves into tax account and stays there. Every invoice = two transactions: business revenue + 25-30% that immediately belongs to government.

topic: Four revenue growth levers in priority order
content:
Most photographers go straight to lever 4 because it feels like progress. Money is in levers 1-3.
1. Raise prices. Highest leverage. Zero additional work. If 20% price raise costs 30% of clients, net revenue still higher and workload lower.
2. Increase transaction size. Upsells, bundles, premium tiers. Same client, same shoot day, larger invoice.
3. Increase purchase frequency. Retainers. Annual refreshes. Quarterly headshot days for corporate clients. Same relationship invoiced multiple times/year.
4. Increase customer count. Marketing. Outreach. New channels. LAST because slowest, most expensive lever and one most photographers pull first.
Three metrics that matter, tracked weekly:
- CLV (Customer Lifetime Value) = avg revenue per booking × avg bookings per client × avg client tenure (years). Corporate headshot at $400/yr × 3 yr = $1,200 CLV. Price first-session offers + acquisition spend against $1,200, not $400.
- CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) = total marketing spend + your time at hourly equivalent ÷ new bookings. If CPA exceeds 15-20% of average booking price, funnel is broken. Either raise prices, reduce spend, or switch channels.
- CR (Conversion Rate) = inquiries converted to bookings, weekly. If CR drops, problem is sales process, not marketing. More inquiries won't fix conversion problem.
Track weekly. Not monthly. Numbers drift slowly enough that weekly catches problems before quarters-long slides.

topic: 3 scaling paths · premium / team / authority pivot
content:
Three paths to break the time-cap. Each produces different economics.
Path A · Premium positioning: Maximize margin per project. Fewer clients, higher prices, better experience. You stay the shooter. Business scales through price, not volume.
- Achieve full capacity at current prices (turning away inquiries, not just feeling busy)
- Identify value gaps. What would justify 30-50% price increase?
- Raise prices 20-50% in one move. NOT 5%/quarter. Single decisive raise.
- Expect 20-40% client loss. Clients who leave were price-shopping. Clients who stay buy outcome and accept premium. Net revenue rises, workload drops.
- Repeat every 12-18 months.
Path B · Team expansion: Maximize volume. Document SOPs, hire associate shooters, retain quality control. You move from shooting every frame to running operation.
- Document SOPs for every phase: intake, pre-shoot communication, shot list, lighting setup, editing, delivery, post-shoot follow-up.
- Recruit associate shooters. Other working photographers who shoot under your brand for day rate.
- Train on SOPs. 1-2 shadow shoots before solo. SOPs are not self-executing.
- Charge client your full rate. Pay associate $300-500/day. Keep margin.
- Quality control: every delivery through you before client sees it. NON-NEGOTIABLE.
Path C · Authority pivot: HIGHEST LEVERAGE. Stop shooting exclusively for clients. Teach the system. Camera becomes distribution engine. Income scales with audience size, not client count.
- Document process publicly. Video breakdowns, written case studies, BTS. Goal isn't content for own sake — extracting system into transferable artifacts.
- Launch education products in sequence (presets first → workflow guides → courses → books → consulting).
- Build email list. Single most important distribution asset.
- Position based on proven client work. Client work = credibility. Education work = leverage.
This is where 10K/mo becomes 30K/mo and eventually 100K/mo. Ceiling is the audience.

topic: Six layers of the Production Stack
content:
Direction Stack covers 90 sec in front of lens. Production Stack covers everything that puts you there.
1. Moodboard · What are we making, visually? → 3-5 page visual brief: title image, tone images, hair/makeup, styling, lighting reference, location reference.
2. Model · Who is in front of camera? → Confirmed subject whose look, availability, comfort match moodboard.
3. Location · Where does this happen? → Scouted space with known light at known time of day, cleared for access, shade and clean background available.
4. Set · What's in the frame beyond subject? → Dressed space. Era filter applied, color palette locked, elevation and depth built in, anachronisms removed.
5. Lighting · How is subject shaped? → Working setup: key, fill, rim, modifiers chosen, grids and flags planned, position marked for pose.
6. Pose · What does body do? → Pose vocabulary fit to subject's body type and comfort. Short vs broad decided. Starting pose + 3 variations.
Sequential — each layer narrows decisions for next. Moodboard narrows style → narrows model → narrows location → narrows set → narrows lighting → narrows posing vocabulary. By the time you arrive on set, decisions remaining are small enough that direction can handle them.
Run in order. Skip none. Don't let later layers bleed into earlier ones.
Direction cannot save what pre-production did not build.

topic: Seven working rules across all layers
content:
1. Specificity beats breadth. Moodboard with 5 images all showing same hard side light + same muted palette beats 30 images that disagree. DM to ONE model who actually fits beats 30 blast messages. Scouted location at 4:30pm in October beats 3 maybe locations.
2. Pre-visit everything that can be pre-visited. Location scouted before shoot. Moodboard reviewed by model. Set dressed day before, not day of. Lighting tested on stand-in or yourself. Every minute of pre-visit saves ten minutes on the day.
3. Light decides everything else. Location chosen for its light. Time of day chosen for its light. Pose chosen so light lands correctly on face. Wardrobe chosen so color holds under the light. When layer decision conflicts with light, light wins.
4. The subject must know what is happening. Send moodboard before shoot. Send call sheet with time, location, wardrobe, mood. Address insecurities BEFORE shoot, not during. A subject who has seen plan arrives in right headspace.
5. Build the library. Every location shot at or driven past → database. Every model → database. Every moodboard, lighting diagram, prop → database. Second shoot in any direction should cost a fraction of first.
6. One thing done well separates the shoot. One intentional element set deliberately apart. One $500 prop in otherwise standard studio. One impossible color. One piece of context competing photographer would never bother to add. Rest can be standard. The one thing carries it.
7. Do not improvise the stack. Skipping moodboard because shoot tomorrow is NOT agile — it's the layer most likely to have caused last shoot to miss. Run the stack every time, even compressed. Compressed stack is still a stack. Skipped stack is a gamble.

3-5 pages, NOT 30 images on one Pinterest wall. Page order matters.
- Page 1: Title image. ONE hero image that makes client think 'this is the photographer.' Single most important page.
- Page 2: Tone. 3-5 images setting emotional register (warmth, tension, formality, playfulness).
- Page 3: Hair, makeup, styling. 2 images per bucket, chosen for consistency of style not variety.
- Page 4: Lighting reference. 3-5 images with same lighting direction, quality, contrast. Team reads as technical brief.
- Page 5: Location reference. 2-4 images of space type or actual scouted location.
For team pages, consistency is the point. Five images all showing hard light is stronger brief than one showing hard light and four showing something else. The repetition makes brief readable.
Tools that matter (just three):
- Pinterest: strong recommendation algorithm. Use Secret boards for client-specific work.
- Cosmos: curated home feed, smaller deliberate source pool. Phone plugin for saving Reels/TikToks.
- Milanote: layout control. Combines mood images + call sheet + outfit inspiration + shot list. Pinterest = where images found; Milanote = where board built.
- Frameset: specialized for commercial work. Indexes stills from commercials, music videos, films.
Working discipline: Save to project, not mega-board. Remove anything that conflicts (not a gallery). Test board with void prompt or reference render. Lock board before outreach.
Delivery: Client gets 3-5 page PDF or shared link with one-line captions. Model gets condensed 2-3 page (title + tone + styling + outfit). Team gets full board + call sheet (stylist gets styling + wardrobe; H&M gets beauty refs + skin/hair specifics lighting demands).

Setup A · Window plus bedsheet:
A window. A white bedsheet hung across to diffuse sun. White wall on shadow side as passive fill. No flash. No stands. Clean commercial-grade soft-light portrait. Bedsheet converts hard midday sun into usable soft light by scattering. White wall fills shadows by bounce. Cost: the sheet and the wall.
Setup B · Two-strobe + diffusion + beauty dish:
Two strobes behind diffusion panel, firing INTO panel rather than directly at subject — produces main soft frontal light. Beauty dish placed above and angled down adds structured top light that sharpens facial architecture. Diffused frontal light = key; beauty dish shapes. Combination reads as editorial without harsh.
Setup C · Classic key + fill + rim:
Octabox as key at 45° to subject, slightly above eye level. Reflector or second softbox as fill on opposite side, 1 stop weaker. Strip softbox with grid behind and above for rim. Works for 90% of commercial portrait assignments. Full control over modeling, shadow density, separation.
Modifier grammar (working set is small, not 20 modifiers):
- Octabox/softbox: default key. 90% of pro portrait.
- Beauty dish: medium-hard, top-down placed above. Reveals facial structure. Beauty + fashion.
- Strip softbox: long narrow source. Elongated highlight. Rim lights + fashion profiles.
- Diffusion panel: neutralizes hardness. Cheap, flexible, essential.
- Grid/honeycomb: narrows beam. Concentrates light into 'pocket'. Prevents rim from flaring lens.
- Reflector: bounces existing light back as fill. Outdoor portraits.
- Negative fill (poly board): absorbs light on shadow side to deepen shadow. Essential for dramatic commercial.
Skin tone exposure: meter for the face. Protect the face. Everything else comes second. For darker skin, +2/3 to +1 stop. For lighter, -2/3 to -1 stop. Meter is wrong on both ends if you let it average.

A pose is 7 independent levers. Working through them in sequence generates new pose in 3 seconds without remembering library of 100 poses.
1. Feet: planted wide, together, tiptoe. Rotated in/out. Foundation.
2. Knee: straight, bent, crossed. Toward camera or away. Bending front knee = most reliable small-change move.
3. Hip: weight centered, or shifted onto one leg. Shifted = waiting-for-bus stance. Less formal.
4. Torso: upright, leaning forward (glorified slouch), leaning back. Forward brings chest/shoulders to camera, pushes gut away.
5. Shoulders: square to camera (confrontational), angled (at ease), fully turned (profile, elegant).
6. Arms and hands: pockets, crossed, at sides, touching face, holding object. Hands in pockets solves what-do-I-do-with-hands for men. For women, one hand at collar or in hair.
7. Head and eyes: chin up/down. Nose toward camera or away. Eyes to camera (connection), past camera (mood).
Adjust ONE point, leave other six. Pose changes. Cycle through all 7 in 2-min session = 20 usable frames without asking subject to 'do something else.'
Male default recovery (untrained males stand square with hands crossed over crotch):
- Turn body toward light source (feet, legs, whole person — not torso only)
- Hands in pockets (THUMBS INSIDE pocket, fingers OUTSIDE pant — not other way)
- Feet close together. Stance narrower than most men think.
- Bend front knee slightly. Single highest-yield adjustment in male posing.
- Lean torso forward (glorified slouch). Chest/shoulders toward camera, gut away.
- Chin forward and slightly down. Reduces double chin, thins jaw.
Female default recovery:
- Shift weight onto one leg. Other leg relaxes.
- Resting leg on tiptoe or slightly bent. Activates knee, produces curve through hip.
- One hand to point on body (waist, collar, hair). Solves arm problem.
- Angle shoulders away from square. Slight rotation.
- Chin slightly down, nose around toward light. Dominant eye closer to lens.
- Eyes commit. Camera, past camera, down, or away. Eyes that wander = uncommitted = image loses.
Rotation trick: 45° rotation from starting pose = new pose. 90° = another. Back to camera with torso twisted toward lens = another. Most photographers stop at one. If out of poses, ROTATE.

T = (C + R + I) / S
- T = Trust
- C = Credibility (technical 'what' · expertise, qualifications, words you say)
- R = Reliability (consistency · doing what you say you'll do · the 'how')
- I = Intimacy (safety client feels in conversations · willingness to share)
- S = Self-orientation (the divisor · the more you focus on yourself, your fee, your needs, your expertise display, the lower the trust)
Self-orientation is the DIVISOR, not a subtractor. Doubling self-focus halves trust regardless of how high credibility goes. Most professionals score high on Credibility but high on Self-orientation, killing trust before it forms.
SNIPED operational implications:
- Direction Stack diagnostic on set IS Credibility
- 5-day SLA + reliable delivery IS Reliability
- 90-second opener and trust-building shoot pre-amble IS Intimacy
- Holding $1,500 cold pricing without justification + refusing 'let me prove I'm worth it' performance IS low Self-orientation
- VIB method is structurally a Self-orientation reducer (the asset/frame comparison talks, the operator does not)
5 trust-building behaviors:
1. Engage · earn the right to discuss the issue (90-second opener)
2. Listen · understand them before being understood (insecurity question on shoot day · 'Anything specifically you're self-conscious about that I should mind?')
3. Frame · re-articulate problem in your own words (protocol diagnostic)
4. Envision · paint the future state (deployment context · 'where will this run?')
5. Commit · ensure they like the solution (gallery delivery + Day-7 testimonial loop)

1. Power of Exposure (Caillebotte's bequest). Two impressionists in 1876 considered equally talented: Monet and Caillebotte. Caillebotte's will donated his collection (including many Monets) to French museums. 140 years later Monet is iconic; Caillebotte barely known. Quality is necessary but not sufficient — exposure is multiplier. Implication: Direction Stack book public launch (Q3 2026) = Caillebotte-bequest move. LinkedIn POV bank cadence = exposure compounding (200 posts over 4 years > 40 posts compressed). Cultural Documentation archive in 10 years IS Caillebotte's bequest.
2. MAYA Rule (Most Advanced Yet Acceptable · Loewy). Pure novelty fails (no entry point). Pure familiarity fails (no surprise). Hit zone = 'aesthetic aha' — new in a way that opens a door to comfort. SNIPED's aesthetic filter (3-of-5 monochromatic/commercial/studio/editorial/graphic) IS the MAYA register. Reset at $1,500 IS MAYA: low enough to clear executive expense card; high enough to signal premium.
3. Force of Story (myth-making mind). Star Wars succeeded as collage of pre-existing myths/templates. Hits = remixes of known patterns. SNIPED's 'engineer-as-operator' identity arc IS archetypal: technical-discipline-meets-creative-craft (Brian Eno, James Dyson, Apple's industrial design lineage).
4. Viral Myth (broadcast not virality). 50 Shades of Grey was Twilight fanfic with built-in audience of millions of FanFiction readers. 'Going viral' = survivor-bias myth. Implication: do NOT plan SNIPED growth on virality. Plan on building broadcast (LinkedIn/IG/Substack) and using it once large enough.
5. Audience of My Audience (clusters, cliques, cults). Smaller densely-connected audience beats larger diffuse one. People share content as '1.25-inch baubles of identity.' LA founder/operator/artist culture IS a cluster, not a market. Optimize for cluster depth, not LA-photographer-market breadth.
6. Economics of Prophecy. Universal McCann predicted iPhone would flop based on 10K-person survey — measurably correct (people honestly didn't know they wanted it) and also wrong (once shown, they did). Job of operator is to ship work that creates new preference. LA founders can't self-diagnose Protocol 3 failure on their LinkedIn header — VIB IS the prophecy: shows what they didn't know they wanted.

topic: Status Anxiety · why founders pay premium (de Botton)
content:
Adam Smith 1759 (quoted Chapter 1): 'To be observed, to be attended to, to be taken notice of with sympathy, complacency, and approbation, are all the advantages which we can propose to derive from [bettering our condition].' Status sought not for material reward but for love. Status = a form of being seen.
Premium portraiture is sold to the part of the founder that wants to be observed, attended, noticed. Product is not the photo. Product is the visibility the photo provides.
SNIPED implications:
- Buyer is not buying pixels. Buying experience of being seen at operational level of their business.
- 90-second on-set opener is critical: operator is performing the act of taking founder seriously, attentively, with respect. Session itself = part of deliverable.
- Pixieset gallery delivery is a moment of being observed. Even before photos deploy, delivery experience IS part of value.
- Op Kit pricing ($3-8K) purchased not for image volume but for deeper attention.
Meritocracy dark side: in modern meritocracies, status depends on individual achievement → failure interpreted as personal moral failing → status anxiety worse. Founder whose visual presence is 'below operational level' experiences as personal failure, not missing service category. The Direction Stack methodology IS shame-relieving — naming as protocol (mechanical, fixable) removes personal-failing interpretation.
Snobbery (engine of premium pricing): premium pricing in service businesses is enabled by buyer's snobbery (not operator's). Operator's job is not to overcome buyer's price-resistance — it's to be priced consistent with buyer's snobbery framework. $1,500 cold quote IS snobbery-aligned for LA founder. $300 commodity headshots fail because too cheap to signal status. Operator NEVER apologizes for price. Premium pricing ENABLES buyer's status signaling.

Foundational text for SNIPED's lane. Read annually.
1. We Will Specialize. Generalists give thinking away because they have no power. Expertise alone is differentiator.
2. We Will Replace Presentations With Conversations. The 'big reveal' addiction is pitch addiction in disguise.
3. We Will Diagnose Before We Prescribe. Four phases: diagnose, prescribe, apply, reapply. Pitching skips diagnostic.
4. We Will Rethink What it Means to Sell. Sell as respectful facilitator, not persuader.
5. We Will Do With Words What We Used to Do With Paper. Proposal is the words from your mouth. Documents are contracts written after agreement.
6. We Will Be Selective. Pursue perfect-fit clients; say no early and often. No is what gives yes power.
7. We Will Build Expertise Rapidly. Once you plant the flag, attacks come. Build proof of expertise faster than attacks.
8. We Will Not Solve Problems Before We Are Paid. Free thinking signals zero-value thinking.
9. We Will Address Issues of Money Early. Set Minimum Level of Engagement; surface before investment compounds.
10. We Will Refuse to Work at a Loss. Margin only diminishes from start. No 'build it now, raise prices later' delusion.
11. We Will Charge More. If not losing on price occasionally, not charging enough.
12. We Will Hold Our Heads High. Seek respect first; money follows respect.
SNIPED tightening: VIB asset replaces presentation; Discovery call IS conversation. 10-protocol Direction Stack IS the diagnostic posture. Free shoot ceiling (4/month) + lane refusal rules ARE selectivity. Direction Stack book Q3 launch IS the proof asset. 'DM SNIPED for the diagnostic' CTA does not give diagnostic away. $1,500 cold quote IS the MLE. $1,500 → $1,800 trigger after booked-out 3 weeks.
Drift risks: 'build cheap to start, raise prices later' trap (resist when zero booked); 'let me prove myself with this one' trap (Direction Stack methodology IS the proof); presentation-as-validation addiction (when zero VIBs converted, urge to 'build a deck' instead of sending VIB #1 is the addiction — SEND THE VIB).

Companion to Win Without Pitching. The pricing playbook for creative service firms.
Core principles:
1. Price the client, not the job. Same scope priced differently for different clients based on value to them.
2. Offer options. Three tiers minimum, anchored high. Never single-price.
3. Anchor high. First number sets the reference. The high option redefines what 'premium' means in conversation.
4. Say a price before you show a price. Verbal price first, document confirms.
5. Master the value conversation. Selling outcomes, not deliverables.
6. Limit unpaid proposals to one page. No multi-page proposal-as-presentation.
Two definitions of premium (load-bearing insight): in sales/marketing, premium = amount paid above ordinary price. In insurance, premium = amount paid for protection against risk. THESE ARE THE SAME THING. Higher-priced options are insurance policies against risk. Most clients buying premium are not buying 'more' — they are insuring against consequences of bad outcome.
SNIPED implication: Op Kit and Brand System tiers are insurance against founder's risk (botched press cycle, deck that fails investors, brand system remade in 12 months). Op Kit pitch language should explicitly name the risk: 'the press cycle is the moment Op Kit was designed for · cost of getting photo wrong at that moment is materially higher than the price of the Op Kit.'
Phase B+ pricing architecture (after first 5 Resets close):
- Reset Standard $1,500 / Reset+ $2,500 (1 location, 5 extra Heroes, license expansion) / Reset Pro $4,500 (full half-day, 3 looks, expanded license)
- Op Kit Standard $4,500 / Op Kit+ $7,500 / Op Kit Brand $12,000
- Brand System Standard $15K / Brand+ $25K / Brand Custom $50K+
'Hold $1,500 cold' is correct as MLE; incorrect as the only price. Phase B+ adds anchored-high options.

A SNIPED frame, at thumbnail size, reads as SNIPED if all 7 signatures hold:
1. Color discipline · monochromatic or strict color-block, locked before shoot
2. Architectural pose · A-frame base, body 35-45° off-axis, chin forward and slightly down, hands with task
3. Rim light always · the silhouette is the moat
4. Clinical retouch · skin unified, pore detail preserved, no plastic smoothing
5. Graphic over atmospheric · shapes and color blocks carry the frame
6. Subject in command · eyes committed before the smile
7. Severity as default · warmth earns its place, never the baseline
A frame that fails 4 of 7 is not SNIPED. This is the editorial standard for HERO tier.
Emotional palette · 7 words that should describe a SNIPED frame:
Composed · Severe · Authoritative · Architectural · Restrained · Operator-grade · Earned
Words that signal drift:
Cute · Cozy · Warm · Trendy · Aesthetic (as noun) · Vibey · Cinematic (used loosely)
Locked Visual Direction (2026-05-12): Quiet luxury editorial restraint. Meisel / Roversi / Mert & Marcus lane. NOT Tadder / jpwphoto cinematic. NOT teal/orange. NOT influencer LUTs.
- Camera profile: Adobe Neutral (v3 LUXURY supersedes v1's Adobe Portrait)
- HEX palette: #2A2A2E shadow · #B8956E skin · #C9B7A3 mid · #F5EFE6 highlight
- Camera body: Canon R6 Mark II
- AI plate cheat codes: Mamiya 7 + Kodak Portra 400

Pressure-tested against drift in a way most photographer businesses are not. Each trap has a corrective.
1. The Influencer Photographer (trendy grades, presets-as-product)
2. The Concert/Tour Photographer Lock-In (camera-for-hire, no body of work)
3. The Wedding/Family/Lifestyle Drift (volume work that doesn't compound)
4. The Hypebeast Editorial / 'Urban Grit' (mistakes shadow for depth)

9. The 'I'm Not a Photographer, I'm an Artist' Cop-Out (refuses commercial ladder)
10. The MFA Art World Drift (refuses commercial as 'selling out')
References beyond photography (cross-medium reference depth most businesses don't have):
- Cinema: Wong Kar-wai (urban color), Barry Jenkins/Laxton (Black portraiture in light), Khalil Joseph (cultural document), Bradford Young (naturalistic environmental), Steve McQueen (austerity), Hou Hsiao-hsien (pacing), Hiro Murai (atmospheric mood), Khalik Allah (documentary ethics)
